summary: The candidate is mathematically correct and complete. Checks at h=1 and h=2, at the boundary x=+/-h, and at cutoff zero reveal no counterexample. The maximum of five affine functions gives a globally finite nonnegative convex potential with the stated failure of evenness. The three original rows give exactly the complete symmetric table and zero weighted mean; its truncation to the convex box satisfies precisely the supplied global-extendability definition, including all zero entries. The total-mass identity and its bound W_h<=3 are exact, and reducing an arbitrary closed cutoff to the preceding attained cost proves existence and the uniform bound for the optimized M_h. Evaluation of all three shifted rows gives the complete shifted-mass formula, including the row evaluated outside Q_h using the globally defined potential. The resulting ratios diverge with h, and the parity count and explicit failure of the same-parity difference estimate are exact. The predecessor facts are used only for their stated conventions and the identified evenness step; no inapplicable even-potential conclusion is invoked.
